fleets.name: Honor
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Honor Device Co., Ltd.). Complements the Huawei fleet, which explicitly excludes Honor.

fleets.name: OPPO
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Guangdong OPPO Mobile Telecommunications). Word-boundary pattern avoids Koppo/Toppower false hits.

fleets.name: vivo
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (vivo Mobile Communication). Full-name pattern avoids Vivotek/Vivox false hits.

fleets.name: Realme
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Realme Chongqing Mobile Telecommunications).

fleets.name: OnePlus
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (OnePlus Technology/Electronics/Tech, Shenzhen).

fleets.name: Meizu
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Meizu Technology). Small assignment count but genuine.

fleets.name: ZTE
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (ZTE Corporation). Covers phones and operator gateways/ONTs.

fleets.name: Nubia
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Nubia Technology, ZTE sub-brand).

fleets.name: Lenovo
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Lenovo entities). Motorola Mobility assignments are split into their own fleet.

fleets.name: Motorola
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Motorola Mobility LLC, a Lenovo Company). Distinct from the Motorola Vigilant law-enforcement fleet.

fleets.name: Xiaomi
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Xiaomi Communications / Beijing Xiaomi Mobile Software / Beijing Xiaomi Electronics). Product-level Xiaomi devices are in the MiBeacon and Theengs fleets.

fleets.name: Aqara / Lumi
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Lumi United Technology, Aqara's parent). Only 2 MA-L blocks exist; most Aqara gear is identified via BLE, not OUI.

fleets.name: Yeelight / Yeelink
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Yeelink, Qingdao — Yeelight's operating entity). Only 1 MA-L block exists.

fleets.name: Roborock
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Beijing Roborock Technology). Most units ship with module-vendor OUIs; this is a supplement.

fleets.name: Dreame
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Dreame Technology / Innovation, Suzhou). Anchored patterns avoid Shenzhen Adreamer.

fleets.name: Midea
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (GD Midea Air-Conditioning / Midea Group). Anchored to avoid Limidea.

fleets.name: Haier
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Qingdao Haier entities).

fleets.name: Gree
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (GREE Electric Appliances, Inc. of Zhuhai). Full-name pattern avoids the many unrelated Green* companies.

fleets.name: Hisense
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Hisense entities; the Hisense Hitachi JV block is MA-M only).

fleets.name: TCL
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (TCL King / Shenzhen TCL New Technology / TCL MOKA et al.).

fleets.name: Skyworth
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Shenzhen Skyworth Digital et al. — operator set-top boxes and TVs).

fleets.name: Konka
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Konka Group / Shenzhen Konka Telecommunication).

fleets.name: Changhong
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Sichuan Changhong Electric et al.).

fleets.name: FiberHome
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Fiberhome Telecommunication Technologies). Major operator gateway/ONT OEM.

fleets.name: Mercury
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Shenzhen Mercury Communication Technologies, TP-Link's budget brand). COMMUNICATION qualifier is mandatory — bare 'Mercury' hits US defense/security firms.

fleets.name: FAST
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Shenzhen FAST Technologies, TP-Link brand). Full-name pattern mandatory — bare 'FAST' is unusable.

fleets.name: H3C
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (New H3C Technologies / Hangzhou H3C / New H3C Intelligence Terminal).

fleets.name: Qihoo 360
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Shenzhen Qihoo Intelligent / Qihoo 360 Technology / 360 AI Technology).

fleets.name: EZVIZ
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Hangzhou Ezviz Software). Hikvision sub-brand with its own IEEE entity; no OUI overlap with Hikvision.

fleets.name: Anker
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L blocks of Fantasia Trading LLC, Anker Innovations' US trading entity — Anker itself has no IEEE entry under its own name. Covers eufy/Soundcore/Anker gear using these blocks.

fleets.name: Baseus
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Shenzhen Baseus Technology).

fleets.name: UGREEN
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Ugreen Group Limited).

fleets.name: Broadlink
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Hangzhou BroadLink Technology / Broadlink Pty Ltd).

fleets.name: Narwal / Yunjing
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Yunjing Intelligent Technology, Dongguan — Narwal's legal entity; IEEE spells it 'lntelligent'). Only 1 block exists.

fleets.name: Xiaotiancai / BBK
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (BBK Educational Electronics, Dongguan — maker of Xiaotiancai/imoo kids watches). Xiaotiancai has no IEEE entry of its own; the imoo substring alone would hit Kiwimoore Semiconductor.

fleets.name: NIO
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (NIO Co., Ltd., Shanghai). Only 1 confirmed block; a second 'Nio' entry (MA-M, San Jose) is unverifiable and excluded.

fleets.name: Espressif module
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Espressif Inc. / Espressif Systems Singapore). MODULE vendor: a hit means the device contains an ESP8266/ESP32 module, NOT that the end product is Espressif-branded. Low specificity by design.

fleets.name: Quectel module
fleets.notes: IEEE MA-L vendor block (Quectel Wireless Solutions). MODULE vendor: a hit means the device contains a Quectel cellular/Wi-Fi module, not a Quectel end product. Low specificity by design.

fleets.name: BTHome device
fleets.notes: Protocol-level match: BTHome v2 advertisement (service UUID FCD2 in the Bluetooth SIG member registry, allocated to Allterco Robotics; BTHome spec at bthome.io). Common for DIY and flashed Xiaomi/Qingping sensors. Identifies the protocol, not a brand.

fleets.name: Chipolo (own network)
fleets.notes: Chipolo's own finder network service FE33 (Bluetooth SIG member registry: CHIPOLO d.o.o.). Complements the name-based Chipolo fleet for units broadcasting without a name. Source: seemoo-lab/AirGuard (Apache-2.0).

fleets.name: Coospo bike computer
fleets.notes: Coospo (酷动) GPS bike computers advertise as CS500-<serial> / CS600-<serial>, with custom services FDA1-FDA4. Source: community Coospo BLE protocol documentation (see data repo CANDIDATES notes).

fleets.name: Eddystone beacon
fleets.notes: Protocol-level match: Google Eddystone beacon (service UUID FEAA, Bluetooth SIG member UUID registry, Eddystone specification). Identifies the beacon protocol, not a brand.

fleets.name: Meross
fleets.notes: Meross devices in pairing mode advertise as Meross-<...> with service data UUID 0xBE30 (GATT service 99e7be30-...). Matching rules are the vendor org's own Home Assistant discovery criteria. Source: meross_rpc (MIT), Meross's official-org community repo.

fleets.name: Xiaomi MiBeacon device
fleets.notes: Protocol-level match: any device advertising the MiBeacon service (FE95, Xiaomi Mi Service, Bluetooth SIG member UUID registry). Specific models are identified by the fleet-mibeacon-* product-ID signatures; this row is the fallback for models not in that table.

fleets.name: Xiaomi / Ninebot scooter (MIScooter)
fleets.notes: Xiaomi/Ninebot e-scooters (M365 family) advertise as MIScooter<serial> and speak MiBeacon (FE95). Source: ninebot-ble scanner.rs (community protocol documentation).

fleets.name: Moat S2 water sensor
fleets.notes: Moat S2 leak/temperature sensor: service data under its 128-bit UUID 00001000-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb (Bluetooth-Devices/moat-ble, MIT); a second advertising form is keyed by manufacturer ID 0x1000 in ble_monitor's parser (MIT) — both forms are included; which one current firmware emits is unconfirmed.

fleets.name: Ninebot / Segway scooter
fleets.notes: Ninebot/Segway e-scooter BLE: names NBScooter*/Ninebot-*/S1D<serial>, plus a proprietary service UUID 6E400001-0000-0000-006E-696E65626F74 ('ninebot' embedded in hex). Sources: ninebot-ble scanner and M365-Rokid-HUD PROTOCOL_FAMILIES.md (MIT), via community protocol documentation.

fleets.name: Pebblebee (own network)
fleets.notes: Pebblebee's own finder network service FA25. Complements the name-based Pebblebee fleet. Source: seemoo-lab/AirGuard tracker definitions (Apache-2.0).

fleets.name: Picooc scale
fleets.notes: Picooc (有品) body scales, broadcast name patterns from openScale's Picooc handler supportFor (GPL-3.0, patterns are factual).

fleets.name: QN protocol scale
fleets.notes: Scales speaking the QN protocol family (used by Qingniu/清牛 and many white-label brands): name contains 'qn-scale' AND advertises AE00 or FFE0. Source: openScale QN handler supportFor (GPL-3.0, facts only).

fleets.name: Samsung Offline Finding
fleets.notes: Protocol-level match: Samsung offline-finding network service FD69 (Bluetooth SIG member registry: Samsung Electronics). Broadcast by Galaxy phones participating in Samsung's offline finding network and by lost devices. Source: seemoo-lab/AirGuard tracker definitions (Apache-2.0).

fleets.name: SwitchBot Curtain 3
fleets.notes: SwitchBot official BLE spec (OpenWonderLabs/SwitchBotAPI-BLE): FD3D service data byte 0 = device type code (ASCII); uppercase = pair/add mode, lowercase = normal broadcast. Theengs fleets cover Bot/Contact/Motion/Blind Tilt/Meter Pro/Outdoor Meter; this type was missing.

fleets.notes: SwitchBot Color Bulb / LED Strip Light / Plug Mini advertise only manufacturer data with company ID 0x0969 (Woan Technology, SwitchBot's parent) and no device-type byte, so the three cannot be told apart from the broadcast alone (official spec: OpenWonderLabs/SwitchBotAPI-BLE). Protocol-level brand match.

fleets.name: ThermoBeacon (additional types)
fleets.notes: Additional ThermoBeacon/Brifit sensor types 0x14 and 0x30 (manufacturer-data leading byte read as pseudo company ID, the same encoding the Theengs WS02-WS08 fleet uses for types 0x10/0x11/0x15/0x18/0x1B). Source: Bluetooth-Devices/thermobeacon-ble DEVICE_TYPES (MIT).

fleets.name: Tilt Hydrometer
fleets.notes: Tilt brewing hydrometer: iBeacon (companyId 0x004C, 02 15) whose UUID A495BB<color>C5B1-4B44-B512-1370F02D74DE encodes the unit color (10 Red, 20 Green, 30 Black, 40 Purple, 50 Orange, 60 Blue, 70 Yellow, 80 Pink). Source: Bluetooth-Devices/tilt-ble (MIT).

fleets.name: TTLock smart lock
fleets.notes: TTLock (Sciener) smart locks advertise their primary service 0x1910; broadcast names look like <model>_<last 3 MAC bytes hex> (e.g. S534_1d22bd). The first two manufacturer-data bytes are a protocol header, not a company ID, so no MANUFACTURER_ID rule is used. Source: roquerodrigo/ttlock-ble (MIT).

fleets.name: Yunmai scale
fleets.notes: Yunmai (云麦) body scales, broadcast name patterns from openScale's Yunmai handler supportFor (GPL-3.0, patterns are factual). The generic ISM* prefix from the same handler is deliberately NOT included (too collision-prone).
